title: Discrepancies of surface temperature trends in the CMIP5 simulations and observations on the global and regional scales
abstract: Abstract. Using the fifth Coupled Model Intercomparison Project (CMIP5) model simulations and two observational datasets, the surface temperature trends and their discrepancies have been examined. The temporal-spatial characteristics for the surface temperature trends are discussed. Different from a constant estimated linear trend for the entire simulation period of 1850–2012, a dynamical trend using running linear least squares fitting with the moving 10 yr time windows are calculated. The results show that the CMIP5 model simulations are generally in good agreement with the observational measurements for the global scale warming, but the temperature trends depend on the temporal change and the regional differences. Generally, contrary to the small discrepancies on the global scale, the large discrepancies are observed in the south- and north-polar regions and other sub-regions.
problem: Climate model simulations (CMIP5) show significant discrepancies in surface temperature trends compared to observations, especially at regional scales like the polar regions, despite showing general agreement on a global scale, which challenges the understanding of their capabilities and limitations.
method: This paper uses a running linear least squares fitting with a moving 10-year time window to calculate dynamical temperature trends, allowing for the examination of temporal-spatial discrepancies between CMIP5 model simulations and observational datasets.
task: The task is to examine and characterize the temporal and spatial discrepancies of surface temperature trends between the fifth Coupled Model Intercomparison Project (CMIP5) model simulations and observational datasets on global and regional scales.
innovation: This paper applies a running 10-year linear trend analysis to CMIP5 simulations and observational data, characterizing temporal-spatial discrepancies and revealing that model-observation agreement is much higher on the global scale than on regional scales, especially in the polar regions.
